VBO:0200666.summary: Bold, energetic and willing to work with a handler, the Heideterrier was developed for the demanding job of flushing wild boar. Its breeding club puts practical hunting ability and stamina at the centre of selection. Karl-Heinz Markhoff and Hans-Werner Jahnke began developing the type in Germany's Lüneburg Heath during the 1970s.
VBO:0200666.shortDescription: A bold, energetic Lüneburg Heath hunting dog, selected for wild-boar work, stamina and cooperation with its handler.

sources.title: Jagdlicher Heideterrier Verein e.V. – Der Heideterrier
sources.evidence: Club home text: courageous, enduring wild-boar specialist with handler attachment and biddability; Markhoff/Jahnke began type in Lüneburger Heide in1970s. Active breeding and test programme is named.

sources.title: Der Heideterrier – Rassestandard
sources.evidence: Own standard VERHALTEN/CHARAKTER: courageous, work-willing, enduring, vital/temperamental, sociable and biddable. VERWENDUNG flushing work; compact45–55cm conformation, slightly rectangular; complete natural tail carried horizontal/slightly sickled (standard also allows docking).
